title: fix(types): combobox `options` and command `groups` are optional on the zod mirror (objectui#6033)
body:
Fixes #6033
Clause-②: yes (C7 / C8 widen the mirror's accept set; the seat reviews at tier before enqueue, per the tier notice `5612085142`)

Implements the last two keys of ruling `5406213903` on objectui#6033 (C7 `ComboboxSchema.options`, C8 `CommandSchema.groups`: "renderer tolerates absence ⇒ mirror goes optional"). The claim's table records the other six keys as landed or superseded elsewhere. Dispatched `os-dev` run in session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01BA3nKVUwKQJf8DBxrSVtNC`, branch `claude/issue-6033-combobox-command-optional`, base `f905090a1`.

## What changed

- `packages/types/src/zod/form.zod.ts`: `ComboboxSchema.options` and `CommandSchema.groups` are now `.optional()`. Nothing else in the file changed (4-line diff).
- `packages/types/src/__tests__/zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`: the two `KnownDrift` rows (`form.zod.ts#ComboboxSchema: 'options'`, `form.zod.ts#CommandSchema: 'groups'`) are removed, one row per key, as the ruling requires. A short note replaces them.
- New pin: `packages/types/src/__tests__/combobox-command-optional-6033.test.ts`.
- `.changeset/6033-combobox-command-optional.md`: `@object-ui/types` **minor**. This follows the precedent for widening this ledger's mirrors, where the group A widenings in `5927-zod-mirror-group-a-widenings.md` also took minor. `changeset:check` gives no other rule, and the fixed group never takes `major`.
- Second commit, `content/docs/components/form/combobox.mdx` and `command.mdx`: `options?` / `groups?`. The section "Beyond the claim's file list" below explains why.

## Re-measured before the edit: the ruling's ground

**Renderer tolerance, rechecked on `f905090a1`.** I wrote a one-shot happy-dom probe under `packages/components/src/__tests__/`, ran it from the repo root and did not commit it. It used two instruments per renderer:
- (a) the real `SchemaRenderer` plus the registry. `SchemaErrorBoundary` turns a throw into a `role="alert"` "failed to render" panel, so each row asserts that no panel appears and that the control's own structure is present.
- (b) the registered component called directly, with no boundary.

| row | combobox (`schema.options \|\| []`) | command (`schema.groups?.map`) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| key absent, (a) | trigger renders with its placeholder, no panel; opening it lists 0 options | cmdk input and empty text render, no panel, 0 `[cmdk-item]` |
| key absent, (b) | no throw, trigger present | no throw, input present |
| control: key present | opening lists `Alpha`, `Beta` | items `One`, `Two` render |
| instrument control: wrong type (`'x'`) | (a) panel appears · (b) throws | (a) panel appears · (b) throws |

Result: `Tests 8 passed (8)`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`. Both renderers draw a node with the key absent, and both instruments detect a throw when one happens. The ruling's ground holds.

**The spec as a third end.** `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0 is the only version in `pnpm-lock.yaml`. Its `ComponentPropsMap` has 45 keys, and neither `combobox` nor `command` is one of them (control: `object-grid` is present). I also scanned the runtime exports of all 17 subpath entry points (2554 names) for `combobox` / `command`. The only hit is `@objectstack/spec/studio` `CommandContributionSchema` (`id`, `label`, `shortcut`, `icon`), which is an IDE command contribution, not this node. So the spec has no props schema for either node that could disagree with the mirror.

**The ledger's type.** Both rows were in `KnownDrift`, the `NarrowerThanDeclared` ledger (the mirror refuses the declared type), marked `OPTIONALITY`. There is no separate required-vs-optional ledger. Removing each pair's single row is the one-row-per-key shrink the ruling asks for.

## The pin, and its ablation

The pin covers:
- the mirror accepting both nodes without the key (and not inventing a default);
- the published `safeValidateSchema` and `StrictAnyComponentSchema` accepting them;
- the key present (empty or populated) as a control;
- a wrong-typed value refused as `invalid_type` on `options` / `groups`, on the mirror and on the root validator;
- a malformed element refused on `options.0.value` / `groups.0.items`, which proves `.optional()` did not loosen the elements;
- the `KnownDrift` block no longer holding either row, with the neighbouring row and both registrations as controls;
- a type-level half, where both faces admit `undefined`.

Ablation: I removed `.optional()` again through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (from objectstack; an anchor that must match, blob hashes, restore from `HEAD`), with the fix committed first:

| mutation | runtime (`vitest`, pin + parity) | restore |
|:--|:--|:--|
| combobox `.optional()` removed | 3 accept rows red, 4 controls green (`3 failed / 41 passed`) | blob `c8c7fb5bf4c2` == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty |
| command `.optional()` removed | 3 accept rows red, 4 controls green (`3 failed / 41 passed`) | blob `c8c7fb5bf4c2` == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty |
| combobox, `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` | 2 errors: the pin's `Expected: undefined, Actual: never`, and the parity ratchet's `Type '"form.zod.ts#ComboboxSchema"' is not assignable to type 'never'` | blob == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty |

On the mutation, anchor matches went from 1 to 0 and the blob went `c8c7fb5bf4c2` → `58a21b67ce98` (combobox) or → `b007cb2358c0` (command). The parity file stays green at runtime under the ablation because its drift ratchet is type-level. The third row shows that ratchet naming the pair again.

## Gates, at HEAD `fcaee38f4`

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/src/__tests__/` plus the five combobox / command renderer suites under `packages/components/src/__tests__/` (`combobox-long-label`, `combobox-option-disabled`, `combobox-schema-members-8140`, `combobox-trigger-type`, `command-item-icon`): `Test Files 245 passed (245)`, `Tests 5307 passed (5307)`. The 245 files are the 240 tracked test files in `packages/types/src/__tests__` plus the 5 suites.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check` (`tsc --noEmit`, examples, `tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0. `--listFilesOnly` confirms that the test program reads both the new pin and the parity file. Its test program reads source only, so no dependency build was needed.
- `pnpm check:control-bytes` OK · `pnpm check:new-line-citations` `0 new citation(s)` · `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` ✅ (1 changeset declared) · `pnpm changeset:check` ✅ (no `major`) · `node scripts/check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` ✅ · `pnpm check:spec-symbols` ✅ · `pnpm check:doc-types` ✅ · `check-doc-example-ids` ✅ · `check-doc-links` ✅ · `check-doc-fence-languages` ✅ · `check-test-path-roots` OK.
- `pnpm check:changeset-claims` (report-only) lists 25 pending changesets that name `form.zod.ts` or the parity file. I read the eight that mention these keys or `KnownDrift`. Each describes its own change at its own revision, and none states that `options` / `groups` are required or gives the current ledger totals. Nothing needed rewording.
- eslint, narrowed to the touched files, with three pieces of evidence:
  1. Which files are in scope comes from `eslint.config.js`: the 3 touched `.ts` files are linted, and the 2 `.mdx` files report "File ignored because no matching configuration was supplied".
  2. `--format json` reports 3 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
  3. Type-aware linting is off. A grep for `projectService|parserOptions|tsconfigRootDir|TypeChecked` in `eslint.config.js` exits 1 (control: `files:` has 9 hits), so this diff cannot change a verdict on an untouched file.
- NOT MEASURED: `check-doc-snippet-types`, exit 2, because its prerequisite (34 unbuilt packages) was not met. Both docs edits are inside `plaintext` fences, and that gate reads only `ts` / `tsx` fences.

## Beyond the claim's file list

The claim lists two drift rows in the parity file, one new pin and one changeset. Three edits go past that list. Each one is forced by this change, and I declare them here so the seat can amend the claim's file surface:

1. **The parity header's pinned figures.** `KnownDrift` goes from 48 entries / 88 keys to 46 / 86. The bullet and its restatement under "KNOWN_DRIFT is a ratchet, not a waiver" are pinned by `the ledger entry counts the header states are derived, not prose` and `the header key totals and cross-ledger figures are derived, not prose`. Removing the rows without updating them turns those pins red. I added the cumulative history sentence the pins ask for and left the earlier history clauses byte-identical.
2. **One live sentence in the same header.** The ratchet section lists "required-vs-optional mismatches" as a class of the ledger. This change empties that class, so a parenthetical now says so and cites this card.
3. **The two docs pages** (separate commit `fcaee38f4`, so it can be dropped on its own). Their schema blocks showed `options` / `groups` as required. Before this change that matched the validator a JSON author meets. After it, the blocks disagree with the declaration, the mirror and the renderer. The dispatch said "stop on breach". The dev contract requires fixing what the change itself falsifies, and allows a bounded in-place fix in the same defect class when no other claim holds the file. I measured that no open pull request touches either page. I took the dev-contract reading and am raising the conflict here rather than choosing silently.

**Seat's answer (`domain:ui` seat #1, in the ACCEPT on objectui#6033):** A. The claim's file surface is extended to all three edits above, including the two docs lines (commit `fcaee38f4` stays). Both lines are in the same defect class, and without them the pages would be the last place still calling the keys required.

## Acceptance notes

- Not filed, recorded only: the `command` renderer spreads leftover schema keys onto the cmdk root `div`. An authored `placeholder` therefore appears as an attribute on that `div` as well as on the input. The probe found it because two elements matched the placeholder text. It is harmless, and none of the filing classes covers it.
- No permanent renderer-side pin for absence was added. The claim allows one new pin, and `@object-ui/types` cannot import React. The probe and its output are quoted above.
